complexity.correctness_reason: sys is never imported, so instantiating PrefixTree raises NameError on __init__ for any input; even with the import added, words longer than the 2000 recursion cap (permitted once the 1000-char limit is lifted) would blow the stack, tying correctness to the NeetCode length cap.
complexity.notes: Slicing word[1:] at every level is unidiomatic and quadratic; passing an index or iterating characters would give O(L). The newly added sys.setrecursionlimit call is both missing its import and recursively fragile — an iterative loop would avoid the depth issue entirely.
complexity.summary: Recursive trie: each node holds a dict of children keyed by single characters plus a terminal flag; insert/search/startsWith recurse on word[1:]. Each recursion level copies the remaining string via slicing, so an operation on a length-L word costs O(L^2); total space is O(T) for T total inserted characters.
